original_question: Can one find a direct proof of the Verlinde formula for dim H^0(SU_X(r), L^k), namely dim H^0(SU_X(r), L^k) = (r/(r+k))^g ∑_{S⊎T=[1,r+k], |S|=r} ∏_{s∈S, t∈T} |2 sin(π(s-t)/(r+k))|^{g-1}, for example by applying Riemann-Roch once the needed Chern numbers of the moduli space are understood?
target_in_paper: §7, Q 5, referring back to §5, Theorem 5: Beauville asks whether one can find a direct proof of the Verlinde formula for H^0(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k), rather than another indirect proof. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the right target very closely: it is Beauville’s Q 5, it states the Verlinde formula itself in essentially the same form as Theorem 5, and it singles out exactly the Riemann–Roch/Chern-number strategy Beauville says he has in mind for a direct proof. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
missing_details: The curve X should be identified explicitly as a compact Riemann surface (so the paper is over ℂ) of genus g, and Beauville says that from this point on he usually assumes g ≥ 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
SU_X(r) should be defined explicitly as the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

The line bundle should be named explicitly as the determinant bundle 𝓛 := O(Θ_L), independent of the auxiliary choice of a degree-(g−1) line bundle L on X; otherwise the symbol L is ambiguous in a stand-alone statement. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

The quantifiers should be made explicit: the question is about the general formula for arbitrary rank r and every integer k ≥ 1, for the given curve X. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

To be paper-faithful, it should be clear that the open problem is not whether the Verlinde formula is true—Beauville presents it as Theorem 5—but whether one can prove it directly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))

If one mentions the Riemann–Roch route, the paper’s equivalent Euler-characteristic version should also be made explicit: H^i(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k)=0 for i>0 and K_{SU_X(r)} ≅ 𝓛^(−2r), so dim H^0(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k)=χ(𝓛^k). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
For full stand-alone precision, the index set in the formula should be described as all decompositions S ⊔ T = {1,…,r+k} with |S| = r. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
refined_question: Let X be a compact Riemann surface of genus g ≥ 2, let SU_X(r) be the moduli space of semistable rank-r vector bundles on X with trivial determinant, and let 𝓛 be its determinant line bundle. For arbitrary rank r and every integer k ≥ 1, can one give a direct proof of Beauville’s Theorem 5, namely dim H^0(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k) = (r/(r+k))^g Σ_{S ⊔ T = {1,…,r+k}, |S|=r} ∏_{s∈S, t∈T} |2 sin(π(s−t)/(r+k))|^(g−1), preferably by computing χ(𝓛^k) directly from the Riemann–Roch formula and the Chern numbers of SU_X(r), rather than by the indirect degeneration or conformal-block methods surveyed earlier in the paper? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, since H^i(SU_X(r), 𝓛^k)=0 for i>0 and K_{SU_X(r)} ≅ 𝓛^(−2r), can one compute χ(𝓛^k) directly by Riemann–Roch and thereby recover the Verlinde formula of Theorem 5? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
justification: This is the exact target because Beauville first states the Verlinde formula as Theorem 5 in §5, then surveys several existing proofs in §§6–7, and finally closes §7 by observing that those proofs are indirect and posing Q 5, whose suggested model is precisely a Riemann–Roch computation of χ(𝓛^k) using the Chern numbers of SU_X(r). Your draft already matches that intent well; the refinement mainly restores the standing hypotheses and notation from §§1–2 so the question is fully stand-alone and paper-faithful. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/alg-geom/9404001v1.pdf))
